You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily｜Trump Imposes Tariffs on Polysilicon; SpaceX & Tesla Launch $16.8 Billion Terafab Project; Non-Farm Payrolls Due Tonight (August 7, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Developments
Musalem: Probability of Inflation Remaining Above Target Rises; Inclined Toward Rate Hikes at Recent Meeting
Fed official Musalem stated that the probability of inflation remaining persistently above target has increased. He was inclined toward rate hikes at the most recent FOMC meeting and believes gradual hikes carry lower costs than sudden large adjustments.
He noted that the U.S. economy has shown resilience in recent months and that pursuing higher GDP through overly accommodative policy would be a mistake.
He also emphasized that future AI -driven productivity gains remain highly uncertain, with risks skewed toward higher inflation.
Market Impact : The hawkish remarks reinforce September rate-hike expectations, exerting near-term pressure on high-valuation tech stocks while supporting the dollar and precious metals.
International Commodities
Trump Says Hormuz Deal Not Yet Formally Reached; Strait “Somewhat Open”
Trump stated that an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz “cannot yet be said to have been formally reached,” but the strait is currently “somewhat open.” The U.S. is participating in negotiations and overall progress is positive.
Iran is advancing a bill on Hormuz passage rules that would ban vessels from the U.S., Israel and other adversarial countries, with fines of up to 20% of cargo value for violations.
A Saudi official said intelligence indicates Iran is planning attacks on Saudi Arabia, with observed drone and missile movements.
Market Impact : Uncertainty around the strait negotiations persists. Oil prices rebounded sharply on Thursday as the geopolitical risk premium rose again, increasing near-term crude volatility.
Macroeconomic Policy
Trump Imposes Tariffs on Polysilicon; Bans Exports of Tungsten and Battery Scrap
Trump signed an executive order under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, setting minimum import prices for polysilicon and its derivatives and imposing an additional 15% ad valorem tariff. The measures take effect on December 4, 2026, and are accompanied by a “Reshore America” incentive program.
The U.S. Commerce Department announced a one-year ban on exports of tungsten scrap and battery scrap, effective August 27, aimed at strengthening domestic critical-minerals supply.
SpaceX and Tesla announced the launch of the Terafab AI chip super-factory project with an initial investment of $16.8 billion.
Market Impact : The tariffs and export bans reinforce supply-chain localization policies, benefiting domestic U.S. industries but potentially raising costs for solar and semiconductor sectors. The Terafab project underscores demand for AI compute self-sufficiency.
II. Market Recap
Commodities FX Performance
Spot Gold : ~$4,252/oz, +0.3%
Spot Silver : ~$61.9/oz, +0.66%
WTI Crude : ~$77.4–77.7/bbl, +2.9% to +3.0%
Brent Crude : ~$82.6–82.8/bbl, +3.9% to +4.2%
US Dollar Index (DXY) : ~99.948, +0.01%
Driver Analysis : Trump’s statement that the Hormuz deal has not yet been formally reached, combined with Saudi warnings of potential attacks, pushed the geopolitical risk premium higher and drove a sharp rebound in crude. Gold consolidated near the $4,300 level after its earlier surge, while silver edged higher. The asset linkage is clear: rising uncertainty over the strait → higher oil → marginal rebound in inflation expectations → renewed discussion of Fed rate hikes, with precious metals oscillating at elevated levels amid the interplay of safe-haven demand and real rates. Near-term commodity moves will depend heavily on the non-farm payrolls data and actual progress on Hormuz.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : ~$64,374, -0.24%
ETH : ~$1,901, -0.24%
Total Crypto Market Cap : ~$2.28 trillion, -0.5%
Liquidations (24h) : Total ~$155 million, of which longs ~$87 million
Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map : Current price around $64,394. The $65,000–$66,000 zone remains a dense short-liquidation area; a sustained breakout could trigger further short covering. Long-liquidation pressure is still significant in the $63,000–$64,000 range. Price is currently near the long/short liquidation watershed, suggesting elevated short-term volatility.
Spot ETF Flows : Yesterday’s net inflow $244 million; current dynamic net inflow ~$9.3 million.
Driver Analysis : Against a backdrop of rising geopolitical risk and mixed U.S. equities, the crypto market held relatively steady. BTC remained above $64,000 while ETH showed limited elasticity. The shift of ETF flows to net inflows provided support, and liquidation volumes stayed manageable. Macro conditions—rebounding oil prices alongside pre-non-farm caution—point to a near-term range-bound crypto market. Attention remains on how the payrolls data will transmit to risk-asset sentiment.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at 53,885.10 (-0.85%), pulled back from record highs
SP 500 : Closed at 7,709.96 (-0.18%), modest pullback
Nasdaq : Closed at 26,348.35 (-0.06%), essentially flat

Performance Summary Driver Analysis : U.S. equities closed lower across the board on Thursday, with the Dow retreating notably from its record high. Microsoft rose nearly 2% and showed relative strength; Nvidia, Apple and Meta posted modest gains. Google continued to face pressure, while Tesla and Amazon edged lower. Pre-non-farm caution dominated sentiment. AI application software stocks weakened broadly, and the memory sector continued to adjust after earlier guidance misses. SpaceX rose more than 6% on the Terafab project announcement.
[...]
1. SpaceX / Tesla – Terafab AI Chip Super-Factory Launched with $16.8 Billion Initial Investment
[...]
Event Overview : SpaceX and Tesla formally announced the launch of the Terafab advanced AI semiconductor complex in Grimes County, Texas, with an initial investment of $16.8 billion. The facility is planned to become one of the world’s largest chip manufacturing sites (over 100 million square feet). It will vertically integrate logic, memory, packaging and testing, primarily serving Tesla’s Optimus humanoid robots, Cybercab and SpaceX’s space-based data centers. Musk described it as “the largest and most valuable building on Earth” and indicated that roughly 25% of future compute output would be allocated to Optimus and 75% to spacecraft AI projects. Market Interpretation : The project directly reflects the Musk companies’ urgent need for AI compute self-sufficiency and underscores ongoing global shortages of advanced chips (particularly leading-edge process nodes and HBM). The $16.8 billion initial outlay is already substantial, with further expansion potential, reinforcing the long-term narrative of vertical integration and in-house capacity. The market views it as a hedge against external reliance on Nvidia and others, while also potentially reshaping parts of the supply chain. Investment Implication : Long-term positive for related equipment, materials and packaging/test supply chains, and strengthens the compute self-sufficiency thesis. Near-term attention should focus on the pressure of large capital expenditure on free cash flow at both companies, as well as project execution timeline and yield-ramp risks.
